study type: Secondary analysis of a cohort study
exposure: HbA1c levels at 8 to < 20 gestational weeks
cohort: 10,001 pregnant women enrolled in the AMANHI cohort between May 2014 and June 2018 across Sylhet-Bangladesh, Karachi-Pakistan, and Pemba Island-Tanzania
finding: Maternal HbA1c level of ≥ 6.5 at early to mid-pregnancy was independently associated with increased risks of stillbirth, preterm birth, and LGA in women from South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa.
